 Immanuel Quickley and Ja’Kobe Walter must deliver as the Raptors chase Knicks payback 
 Toronto’s starting backcourt has to be better. By Amos Caesar Mina | Nov 17, 2026, 3:15 PM EST Share on Facebook Share on X Share on Reddit Copy Article Add us as a preferred source Oct 3, 2026; Quebec City, Quebec, CAN; Toronto Raptors guard Immanuel Quickley (5) looks on against the Miami Heat during the second quarter at Videotron Centre. Mandatory Credit: David Kirouac-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect It’s right back to work as the Toronto Raptors host the New York Knicks once again later tonight. Their first tilt was an overtime thriller, although it definitely stung for Raptors faithful to watch Toronto collapse late and let New York claw its way back into the game.
--> It’s right back to work as the Toronto Raptors host the New York Knicks once again later tonight. Their first tilt was an overtime thriller, although it definitely stung for Raptors faithful to watch Toronto collapse late and let New York claw its way back into the game.
 Heading into tonight’s rematch, I’ll be paying close attention to Toronto’s starting backcourt tandem: Immanuel Quickley and Ja’Kobe Walter. At the time of writing, Scottie Barnes (who played the hero for much of Toronto’s push against the Knicks) is listed as questionable with an illness . If that turns into a late scratch by tip-off, it’ll only put more responsibility on Quickley and Walter’s shoulders, alongside another key Raptor, RJ Barrett, who stood out last game … for all the wrong reasons .

 Consistency from the backcourt is a must for Toronto in rematch vs. Knicks
--> Consistency from the backcourt is a must for Toronto in rematch vs. Knicks
 IQ finished Sunday night with 17 points, six assists, six rebounds, and two steals. Decent numbers, sure, but his efficiency left a lot to be desired: he shot 38.9 percent from the field (7-for-18).
--> IQ finished Sunday night with 17 points, six assists, six rebounds, and two steals. Decent numbers, sure, but his efficiency left a lot to be desired: he shot 38.9 percent from the field (7-for-18).
 Thankfully, Jamal Shead stepped up in a big way, filling the gaps with an efficient 19-point performance. That energy and effort on offense are exactly what Raptors fans would love to see more consistently, as it’s one of his biggest obstacles to earning a larger role . Still, IQ is slotted as this team’s lead guard, and he’s expected to be one of its key shooting threats and contributors , while keeping the offense running smoothly.

Still, IQ is slotted as this team’s lead guard, and he’s expected to be one of its key shooting threats and contributors , while keeping the offense running smoothly. 
 Quickley, like his “BBQ” faction mate RJ Barrett, is another one of those guys who gets flak for trying to do too much or having weak court vision— missing the right read, passing up the extra pass to hunt for a rushed shot, or fumbling the possession altogether. 
--> Quickley, like his “BBQ” faction mate RJ Barrett, is another one of those guys who gets flak for trying to do too much or having weak court vision— missing the right read, passing up the extra pass to hunt for a rushed shot, or fumbling the possession altogether. 
 But if IQ can stay poised, shoot at a decent volume, and tone it down when things aren’t going his way, the focus shifts to whether he can be a steady presence at the point and help his squad win. Forcing shots in isolation or taking on multiple defenders has become too much of a recurring theme for IQ, and he needs to clean it up urgently. It’s for the team’s greater good.

 Then, on the other side of this conversation, we’ve fallen right back into the same discussion I raised about Ja’Kobe Walter not too long ago . 
--> Then, on the other side of this conversation, we’ve fallen right back into the same discussion I raised about Ja’Kobe Walter not too long ago . 
 After snapping out of his slump with a strong showing against the Celtics last week, Walter’s inconsistency has surfaced again: he went 1-for-6 from deep against the Knicks and is 2-for-12 from three over the past two games. His defensive upside helped keep him on the floor, but it still hurts when one of your key X-factor players has a rough shooting night.

His defensive upside helped keep him on the floor, but it still hurts when one of your key X-factor players has a rough shooting night. 
 Meanwhile, the Knicks had an absolute spark plug in Landry Shamet, who scored 23 points on 66.7 percent shooting (8-for-12 overall, 4-for-7 from deep) and delivered crucial buckets down the stretch to help push New York over the edge.

 Walter simply has to maintain the strong defense he brings to his game while getting his scoring back to the level that showed so much potential coming out of last year. The move into the starting lineup may have come a little too quickly, taking away some of the spark he brought off the bench (a role he’s likely better suited for). 
--> Walter simply has to maintain the strong defense he brings to his game while getting his scoring back to the level that showed so much potential coming out of last year. The move into the starting lineup may have come a little too quickly, taking away some of the spark he brought off the bench (a role he’s likely better suited for). 
 But Toronto has little choice right now but to lean on him with the starters. Serviceable defense alone won’t cut it: the Raptors need extra buckets and quality possessions from Walter when games get tight, or when they need a hot blitz to build an early run.

 And while this is key to beating New York tonight, don’t get it twisted: Toronto can’t afford to let IQ and Walter take their foot off the gas after this matchup. I want to see them keep improving through the next stretch of games — and be ready to remain difference-makers upon Kawhi Leonard’s eventual return.
